claims.text: www/index.html at stage-0 contains an h1, a p, and a ul of three li/a links, with no <style>, no <link rel=stylesheet> and no <script> element.
Browsers apply default (user-agent) styles to HTML with no author CSS, e.g. larger bold headings and coloured, underlined links.
claims.source_hint: MDN: Introduction to CSS / cascade (user-agent stylesheets); HTML spec rendering section

claims.text: The <title> element sets the document title shown in the browser tab; <head> holds metadata, <body> holds the page's content.
JavaScript is attached to a page with a <script> element and can change the page after it has loaded (react to events, change content) without a new page load.
Following a plain HTML link makes the browser request the link's address and load a new page.
Caddy serves www/index.html at http://localhost:8080/index.html in the lab.
In most browsers Ctrl+U or right-click → View page source shows the page's original HTML source.
HTML describes structure, CSS describes appearance, JavaScript adds behaviour; each has one job.

Without JavaScript a page still has built-in browser behaviour (following links, CSS hover styles, CSS animations), but running custom logic on a click and changing the page in place requires JavaScript.
